headline.purpose: Results count heading and empty-result line; builder step headings at 1.875rem.

title.purpose: Cartel lead-in, store group headings, panel headings.

lead.purpose: The single explanatory paragraph on home, max 32rem.

label.purpose: Toggles, segmented options, chips, footer, status lines.

micro.purpose: Axis ends, column heads, price differences, tags; tabular.

display-section.purpose: Opening heading of a secondary page or band (Armá tu PC; the home band a step smaller), uppercase.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: The only lift: under the rotated fluo cartel (verdict and build total) and the blank home card.

shadows.name: tape-contact
shadows.purpose: Contact shadow of the paper tape strip on a cartel; part of the card, not a second elevation.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The easing curve for every animation except the hanging tag's pendulum.

motion.name: write-in
motion.purpose: A new verdict price is written left to right.

motion.name: strike
motion.purpose: The marker stroke cancels a beaten price.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Arriving result rows and arrival-order entries.

motion.name: slap
motion.value: 560ms translateY(-14px) scale(1.07) to rest, overshoot at 60%
motion.purpose: The cartel lands on the wall.

motion.name: swing
motion.value: 4.5s ease-in-out infinite rotate(-5deg to 6deg), origin top
motion.purpose: The hanging price tag on home.

motion.name: marker-pass
motion.value: 1500ms after 250ms, left -2% to 78% with fade in/out
motion.purpose: The marker crosses the home example while strikes draw at 350ms and 850ms.

motion.name: cartel-morph
motion.purpose: The cartel travels between home and /armar as one object (shared name cartel).

motion.name: part-enter-3d
motion.value: 0.75s seat-in with slight overshoot, from the part's real direction, 0.18s stagger; case scales 97% to 100% on quartic ease-out
motion.purpose: A chosen part slides into its place in the 3D case.

motion.name: camera-focus-3d
motion.purpose: Camera moves to the current step's part; overview for case, summary, and home.

motion.name: power-on-3d
motion.value: exponential ramp at 2.2/s: fans spin, light strips and interior light rise
motion.purpose: The PC powers on once all seven parts are in.

motion.name: idle-sway-3d
motion.value: camera azimuth oscillation on the glass side: cos(t*0.32), wide on home; cos(t*0.5), barely perceptible in the builder
motion.purpose: Slow idle sway so the model reads as 3D; drag orbits instead.

motion.name: step-progress
motion.purpose: Ink fill of the step rail track.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none; strikes drawn fully; marker hidden; view transitions instant; 3D parts placed instantly, fans still, no sway, camera cuts; drag only

focus.purpose: Global focus; paper outline on the ink top bar; search fields use a 3px fluo ring on focus-within.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Fluo Price Card"**

The system is the Argentine shop-window price card (cartel flúo) laid on a cool sheet of card stock. One hot pink card carries the answer: a monumental, narrow, black price in Archivo at 62% width and weight 900. When a cheaper store answers, a marker stroke strikes the old price and the new one is written in left to right. Everything around the card is quiet ink on paper: hairline rules, flat white sheets, tabular numbers, small round store dots.

Density is that of a working comparison tool, not a landing page. The verdict is loud and singular; the evidence (per-store minimums, the price strip, the result list) is calm, ruled, and scannable. Color is spent on meaning, never on decoration: pink is the card, lime is "cheapest", the store colors are identity dots, red is failure.

The world is light-only (`color-scheme: light`) and rejects dark neon "gamer" surfaces, glow, and grids of equal product cards.

The world extends to a PC builder (`/armar`) without changing its materials: the build total is the same pink cartel corrected live with the same marker strike, and the parts sit in 3D as a real machine in physically based materials, with the cartel layer on top: the part being chosen outlined in pink, missing parts as dashed ink ghosts, ink outlines and an ink price tooltip on hover. Around the card live a few physical cartel objects: paper tape, a hanging price tag, the marker.
keyCharacteristics: One rotated fluo pink card per screen, lifted off the paper by the system's only shadow.
Two widths of one family: condensed black for prices, normal width for everything else.
Hairline-ruled lists and flat white sheets instead of cards and shadows.
Lime marks the winner; store colors appear only as round dots.
Motion is handwriting and paper: strike-through and write-in, the card slapped onto the wall, parts sliding into the case, all on the ease-out-expo curve.
3D is a hybrid: realistic materials inside the case, the cartel's pink and ink drawn on top as outlines, ghosts, and a price tooltip.

rules.name: The Cartel Rule
rules.body: Pink is the card's material. It appears on the cartel (verdict or build total), on the blank card that asks for the query, on the controls that produce a cartel (logo, top-bar search submit, search focus ring), on text selection, and on the outline of the one 3D part being chosen. Never a section background, never a text color, never on a list row, never a status. A search that does not produce a cartel (a builder step) submits in ink.

rules.name: The Lime Means Cheapest Rule
rules.body: Lime marks the lowest price or the money saved, and nothing else. "Compatible" is not lime: it is ink text with a check.

rules.name: The Neutral Stores Rule
rules.body: Store colors never fill a surface, tint text, or color a border. Every store gets the same 10px dot (with a 1px ink/15 ring so yellow survives on white), so no store is favored beyond its price.

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: Every price, the hero, page and band display headings, step numbers, and the budget input run in the narrow black cut with tabular lining numerals; nothing else does. Body and UI stay at normal width. No second family.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that is compared (prices, counts, response times, differences) is tabular.

rules.name: The Only Lifted Thing Rule
rules.body: If it is not the pink card (or the tape holding it), it is flat. Panels, rows, toggles, buttons, the 3D well, and the mobile total bar carry no shadow.

rules.name: The Hybrid Build Rule
rules.body: Inside the case the PC is rendered; on top of it, the cartel annotates. Parts use physically based materials at real scale (1 unit = 10 cm): near-black case steel, darker and lighter steel, brushed aluminum, dark and deep-green circuit boards, matte black and grey plastics, gold contacts, a perforated mesh front, printed labels, and a tempered-glass side (clear, 7% opacity, full clearcoat). Light is a studio: ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure 1.2, a neutral room environment at 0.95, a white key light with soft shadows, a cool rim from behind, and a hemisphere fill grounded in Hairline. The cartel layer is flat lines over the render: the active part's box in solid fluo pink (dashed pink while it is missing), missing parts as dashed ink ghosts at 32%, an ink box on hover (never for the case), and an ink "Name · $price" tooltip. Light inside the machine is white only and appears only when all seven parts are in. No pink, lime, or store colors on materials, no colored RGB lighting, no bloom, no dark stage; the canvas stays transparent over Sheet (the well, or the home band).

dos: Do keep exactly one pink card per screen, rotated a degree or so, with Card Lift and tape.
Do render 3D parts in real materials with the cartel layer on top: the active part outlined in pink, missing ones as dashed ink ghosts, hover in ink.
Do mark compatibility in ink with a check, incompatibility in alert red with the triangle.
Do set every price in Archivo `wdth 62` weight 900 with tabular lining numerals.
Do cancel a beaten price with the marker strike and write the new one in, never by swapping text silently.
Do put data on Sheet panels and ruled lists with 1px Hairline dividers.
Do show every store with the same 10px dot and its `meta.ts` color.
Do keep Pencil small text on Sheet; on Card Stock use Graphite.
donts: Don't use pink for backgrounds, text, statuses, or list rows outside the cartel, its search controls, and the active 3D part.
Don't use lime for anything that is not the cheapest price or the savings, including "compatible", "chosen", or "done".
Don't fill surfaces, tint text, or color borders with store colors.
Don't add shadows or glows to panels, rows, buttons, or the 3D well.
Don't put pink, lime, or store colors on 3D materials, or add colored RGB lighting, bloom, or a dark stage behind the canvas.
Don't introduce a dark theme, neon glow, or a grid of equal product cards.
Don't add a second typeface or use the narrow cut for running text.
